newsitem.title: NEPAL: New Nepal PM to face confidence vote on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: New Nepal PM to face confidence vote on Wednesday.

text.p: Nepal's one-week-old coalition government headed by Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand will face a vote of confidence in parliament on Wednesday, officials said on Monday.

"A formal notice has already been given to the parliament secretariat (by Chand) and the motion will come up for discussion and voting on Wednesday," Ishwar Prasad Upadhyaya, parliament secretary-general, told Reuters.
Chand, of the centre-right Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) was appointed prime minister last week after the resignation of the previous prime minister, Sher Bahadur Deuba.
Deuba resigned after his centrist Nepali Congress-led government lost a crucial vote of confidence in the 205-seat parliament.

The defeat was caused by a split in the RPP, whose breakaway leader Chand became the new prime minister with support from the Congress party's arch-rival, the communist Unified Marxist Leninist (UML) party.
Chand, heading the Himalayan kingdom's second coalition government in 18 months, is required by the constitution prepared in 1990 to prove his majority within 30 days.
Chand whose RPP commands only 20 deputies, has been supported by the UML, which controls 90 votes, and minor allies.
